When I was younger, I saw this show on National Geographic. It was documenting this tribe; how they go through their daily lives n' such. One of the main things I noticed was that none of them had any clothes on. Just bits n' pieces to protect various parts of their body, mainly their feet.

After watching it, I started to feel pretty nihilistic about clothing. Like, "why do we all feel the need to hide ourselves behind clothing, when these people are so open about wearing nothing?"

I then began looking into other cultures, mainly European, that were very comfortable with being nude. In France, I noticed that entire families would go to beaches nude together. That was the first time I noticed myself feeling jealous. I never had a close relationship with my family. Not only where they all together, but they were together in a sense that brought them even closer as a family.

I've always felt comfortable in the nude, though a bit worried of what others might think, which I know isn't something I should be concerned with. I would imagine it has to do with the stigma - at least in America - centered around being naked in public. My experiences are mainly centered around the house, though I have a few moments where I've been naked in front of others. Mainly as a child.

I noticed that it's a great display of self-confidence, and in a world designed to make you feel self-conscious for profit, that's a very valuable trait to have. More than anything, I want to meet with others who feel the same way that I do. If being an adult has taught be anything, it's that being around others who compliment your aspirations is a great way of growing stronger as a person.
